escalation.question: When a client goes over the rate limit, what should happen?
escalation.context: The ticket says "limit bursts to protect the API" but doesn't define the over-limit behavior. I've built the limiter middleware and tested the under-limit path — this one decision is all that's blocking the rest. I won't guess on something that changes the API's public contract.

options.desc: Clear to clients and easy to reason about. Can feel harsh during legitimate spikes.
Absorbs short bursts without errors. Adds latency and some memory pressure under load.
Fair, industry-standard, predictable. Slightly more to implement — I can do it in this loop.

openPRByWorkspace.title: Add OAuth provider config + secrets handling

summary.html: Adds Apple and Google sign-in to checkout. Provider config and secret handling ship in this PR; the sign-in buttons in the checkout UI follow in #483.

items: New OAuth provider registry in auth/oauth.ts for Apple + Google.
Client secrets now resolved from the secrets manager at startup — never read from process.env or logged.
Session/token refresh extracted into a reusable useOAuthSession hook.

summary.html: Key decision: tokens are stored in an httpOnly cookie rather than localStorage, so they're not reachable from JS. Flagging because it changes how the client reads auth state.

focus.title: Where to focus your review
focus.body: The token-refresh race in useOAuthSession.ts (lines 5–10) is the subtle part — two tabs refreshing at once. The Reviewer added a mutex; worth a human look.
